facts.text: Toronto singer, songwriter and producer 11:11 blends R&B and trap in his melodic recordings.
80 Empire is the Canadian songwriting and production duo of Adrian and Lucas Rezza. Their music combines hip-hop with soul, funk and soulful house music.
80 Empire has produced music for Maestro Fresh Wes, Divine Brown and Reema Major.
Québec artist Aswell blends emo rap, pop and folk music with melodic flows and introspective writing. His projects include the 2021 EP Solo and the 2024 album Banlieue.
Toronto rapper Adam Bomb developed through freestyling and battle rap. He is a member of Freedom Writers and Naturally Born Strangers, and his solo writing includes personal storytelling.
Adam Bomb has collaborated with Maestro Fresh Wes and D-Sisive.
Toronto R&B singer anders uses trap-adjacent production on Free Myself from his 2021 project Honest. The record explores self-reflection and relationships.
PARTYNEXTDOOR blends R&B songwriting with trap production on his 2013 self-titled debut, which features Drake on Over Here.
Rouyn-Noranda rapper Anodajay founded Disques 7ième Ciel in 2003 to release Premier VII. The label subsequently released the debut albums of Samian, Koriass and Dramatik.
Ottawa rapper DL Incognito described Organic Music for a Digital World in 2006 as sample-driven hip-hop production built from record breaks rather than keyboard compositions.

Montréal rapper and beatmaker Calamine writes political rap about social justice, housing and ecological issues. Her live collaborators include co-producer Kèthe Magané and saxophonist Valérie Lachance-Guillemette.
Ottawa rapper City Fidelia released Freedumb in 2016, City of Lost Angels in 2017 and Painkiller in 2022.
Begonia combines synth-pop and soul in autobiographical songwriting. Her debut album Fear was co-produced with Matt Schellenberg and Matt Peters of Royal Canoe.
Royal Canoe makes pop with keyboards, sample pads, guitars, drums and effects pedals.
Royal Canoe recorded Sidelining in 2021 by developing ideas together in the studio.

Bodywash is the Montréal duo of Chris Steward and Rosie Long Decter. Their musical references include dream pop and shoegaze, with Steward drawing on British guitar music and Long Decter on folk and Canadiana.
Blonde Diamond explores dream pop, indie pop and indie rock on Magnetic Strangers.
Ellis is Hamilton songwriter Linnea Siggelkow. Her project began in 2017, and the dream-pop EP The Fuzz preceded her confessional full-length album Born Again.

Sister Ray is the songwriting project of Ella Coyes, whose musical background includes gospel, bluegrass and traditional Métis music. Their songs explore trauma, obligations and freedom through personal storytelling.
Beverly Glenn-Copeland recorded Keyboard Fantasies in 1986 using a DX-7 synthesizer and TR-707 drum machine. Its electronic sound connects new-age music with early techno experiments.
Monsune identifies the musical references for Nothing in Return as electronic music, R&B, soul, neo-psychedelia and plunderphonics.
Canadian rapper and producer Night Lovell emerged during the mid-2010s cloud-rap movement with brooding production and inventive music.
Busty and the Bass explores soul, funk, jazz and dance music. The group collaborated with Magi Merlin on Far From Here.
